title: docs + skills: state the bounds of a hook transaction (nested transaction() refused in the sandbox, unit not ambient, ledger carve-out, PostgreSQL abort)
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ

Filing gate: ② out-of-scope finding from the contract review of PR #35309 (record 6999973886, out-of-scope note 1 plus nits N2 and N3), named for a card there. ⛔ Not a claim. p3: the failure is loud, so this card is not dispatched alone; it rides a same-file p2 PR.

## What happens (read from code by the review, not run)

- A `ctx.api.transaction` nested inside another one in the same sandboxed body is refused: `packages/runtime` sandbox `quickjs-runner.ts:806-807` throws `nested ctx.api.transaction is not supported`. No test pins it, and no doc or skill says it. `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx:373-374` and the new skill row in PR #35309 both say a nested transaction "joins" with no bound, so an author is now more likely to nest.
- A unit a sandboxed body opened itself is never ambient. The trio does not publish into the store (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:6681-6693`; the one publisher is `engine-transactions-section.ts:177`), and the write door opens none under a threaded handle (`engine-hooks-and-functions.ts:538-539`). So a hook's `ctx.api.transaction`, fired by a write inside an action body's transaction, opens a second driver transaction instead of joining.
- Not stated anywhere a hook author reads: a lifecycle-classed ledger (`audit`, `telemetry`, `event`) on another datasource is written outside the transaction, not refused (`engine-execute-transactions.ts:318`, `transaction-errors.ts:144-147`); on PostgreSQL a failed statement aborts the whole unit even when the body catches the throw (`hooks.mdx:347-354`); a driver with no transactions degrades silently.

## Do

1. Add a test that pins the nested refusal (`quickjs-runner.ts:806-807`).
2. Bound "joins" in `hooks.mdx:373-374` and in the hook skill row PR #35309 adds: one level only in one body, and a body's own unit is not joined by writes it triggers.
3. Name the ledger carve-out, the PostgreSQL abort and the no-transaction degrade beside it.

Land after PR #35309 merges (same skill row).
